message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average; varies with isotope) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Molecular form** | H₂ (diatomic) under normal conditions |
| **Boiling point** | –252.9 °C (20.4 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| **Color** | Colorless |
| **Odor** | Odorless |
| **Taste** | Tasteless |
| **Solubility in water** | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C (low) |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (4–75 % H₂ in air) |
| **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides with metals; reacts with halogens, oxygen, and many other elements; participates in acid–base chemistry as a proton donor (H⁺). |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H, D), Tritium (³H, T) – each with distinct nuclear properties. |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Standard enthalpy of formation (gas)** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| **Standard entropy (gas)** | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| **Standard molar volume (gas)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ at 0 °C, 1 atm |
| **Acid–base behavior** | Acts as a weak base (forming hydride H⁻) or strong acid (donating H⁺) depending on context. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – fundamental to astrophysics. |
| **Role in biology** | Essential component of water, organic molecules, and metabolic processes; fuels cellular respiration. |
| **Industrial uses** | Fuel cell technology, ammonia synthesis (Haber process), petroleum refining, metal production, semiconductor manufacturing. |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: lowest density, low boiling/melting points.
- **Highly reactive**: forms compounds with almost all elements; key in acid–base chemistry.
- **Isotopic diversity**: deuterium and tritium used in nuclear fusion research and tracer studies.
- **Energy carrier**: central to hydrogen fuel cells and clean‑energy initiatives.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
